Commentary.Commentary: As for the bowling, Vishwa Fernando started the charge and picked up 3 wickets in all. Kasun Rajitha also picked 3 of his own, whereas the part-timers in Dhananjaya de Silva and Dimuth Karunaratne picked up 3 between them. The fielding was a slight let-down, with 3 catches being dropped. Maybe the hosts could have been bowled out earlier otherwise but the Lions will not mind this either. They will look to bat well now and see off the remainder of the day with not much loss in terms of wickets. Let's see how it pans out... Back in 10!

Sri Lanka would have taken this with more than open hands at the Toss. They have bowled out South Africa for 222 after the hosts won the coin flip and elected to bat first. The start was a really bad one for the Proteas as they were 15/3 at one stage before a recovery of sorts happened by Du Plessis and Markram. The skipper fell at the stroke of Lunch but the latter continued to make a fifty. When Markram fell and Mulder followed soon after, it looked like the home team would not breach the barrier of 200. They got there, only due to the heroics of De Kock who made 86 runs off just 87 balls. He batted brilliantly and got support in the form of Rabada. Once he fell though, soon after Tea, not too many runs were added and the away team wrapped up the innings at 222.

OUT! Caught! Good length delivery around off, Olivier looks to defend it but gets an outside edge and the ball goes behind to the keeper. It is a very simple catch for Niroshan Dickwella behind the stump who takes it comfortably. There is a review left but Olivier does not take it as it was an obvious edge. South Africa are bowled out for 222.
Full length delivery on off, Duanne defends it off his front foot.
Well kept out by Steyn to end a successful over by Dhananjaya.
Olivier is beaten outside off first ball. The batsman fails to put bat on ball as it keeps straight. One run added to the total. Bye signaled by the umpire as the batsmen switch ends.

OUT! There is a slight murmur just as the ball goes past the bat and that is enough evidence for the third umpire to ask the on-field umpire to stay with the original decision. A flatter and quicker one full outside off, Rabada goes for the drive but does not make the contact he wanted to. Dickwella collects it and appeals, the umpire raises his finger. Rabada does not think he hit the ball and goes up for a review. The Snicko though shows us a small murmur as the ball passes the bat. The third umpire asks the on-field umpire to stay with the original decision. One to go now...
Review time... Rabada has been given out caught behind here but goes up immediately. Let's see what the replays have to say. Was it bat hitting ball or bat hitting ground?

An off spinner on middle and leg, spins further down the leg side. Steyn misses his flick and Dickwella collects it well. A slight appeal but the umpire says not out.
A flighted ball on middle, defended with the straight bat by Steyn.

Bouncer! Dale ducks under it and lets it go.
Almost bowled him there! A slow yorker attempted but it goes full and just over the bails. Steyn was way too early into that shot and was beaten all ends up.
Worked off his pads this time by Steyn but for no run.

Lands it on a length, Kagiso blocks it off his back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

De Kock was expecting it to spin in and was looking to hit it inside-out towards cover but he misses and the ball goes straight on to hit the off pole. We are back for the final session of play. Quinton De Kock and Kagiso Rabada to continue batting. The former will be on strike and will face Vishwa Fernando first up. Meanwhile, we also find out that Lasith Embuldeniya has gone to the hospital to get his thumb checked. Doesn't sound too good...
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

The visitors' bowling has been really good, especially Kasun Rajitha. The same cannot be said about their fielding though. Three catches have been put down till now, which if not dropped could have possibly seen the end of the Proteas' innings. The bowlers will look to enjoy a good 20-minute break and then come back to wrap up the remaining 3 wickets as soon as possible. Will they do so or will QDK and the tail frustrate the Lankans? Join us in a while for the 3rd session to find out...

Another good session for the visitors! The second period started off with the hosts putting up some quick runs courtesy Quinton de Kock and Aiden Markram. The latter though fell soon after his fifty and just before the Drinks break. Debutant Wiaan Mulder played a couple of really good-looking shots before getting out. Keshav Maharaj who then walked out did not last long either. De Kock has carried on his merry way though and made a good fifty of his own. With the support of Kagiso Rabada, he will look to take the South African total to as much as possible.

Dropped! Ahh... Lakmal nearly had that one. QdK has been put down. That would have set the cat free amongst the pigeons for sure, because there isn't much batting to come! But to be honest, it was not easy. Good length delivery around off, de Kock went for a push but got a thick outside edge. The ball went to Kusal Mendis at second slip who dived to his right and got his hand to it but could not hold on. The ball then went towards the third man region and they took a couple. They say the more you look at a thing, the more deceptive it becomes. More and more replays and we are now not sure whether the ball carried to Mendis. Let us play safe then. Half-chance? But this could be a big moment in the game. De Kock can make them pay.

Drinks are on the field. The last few minutes of the session has just suddenly changed the way the play was going. Quinton de Kock and Aiden Markram were building a solid partnership but Rajitha has brought the downfall of the opener as well as the man who walked in to bat next, Wiaan Mulder. Sri Lanka surely on top here and would like to skittle the lower order quickly. Meanwhile, Keshav Maharaj is the new man in for the Proteas and will look to build a good stand with QDK.

Welcome back for the Post-Lunch session. It has been an exciting beginning to this second and final Test. The away side are in a good position and will look to strengthen it even more with quick wickets in the second session as well. Aiden Markram has been joined in the middle by Quinton de Kock who will face the first ball of the session that will also the last ball of Karunaratne's over. Let's resume...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The visitors are clearly on the front foot here and will look to continue this superb performance in the next session as well. But they need to be cautious too. They had the Saffas 89/4 in Durban but then  let the noose loosen a little. They will be looking to get into the Mulders and the Maharajs and the bowlers soon and who knows - probably bat sometime in the evening, if things go their way. The post-Lunch session begins at 1240 local time (1040 GMT). Join us for it...

What an end to this session that has surely belonged to Sri Lanka. They started the day by losing the toss but bowled tight lines and kept troubling the South African batsmen. Vishwa Fernando's double blow put the hosts on the back foot and things got from bad to worse when Temba Bavuma got run out for the second time in this series. Aiden Markram and his skipper Faf du Plessis joined hands and were steadying the ship but their 58-run stand was broken just before Lunch when Dimuth Karunaratne's yorker got the better of his counter-part.

OUT! BOWLED! Would you believe it? Would you believe it? Asking again. Karunaratne has struck. Just his second wicket in Tests after grabbing his first way back in August 2017, when he had trapped India's Cheteshwar Pujara LBW in Colombo. Faf has been cleaned up by a yorker. But a 104 kph yorker. It was around middle and off and the Protea skipper was very late in getting his bat down. Perhaps he looked to drive initially. Then realized the length and wanted to dig it out. This indecision costs him time and the ball goes under the bat and hits the off stump. It was Faf du Plessis who was dismissed at the stroke of Lunch on Day 1 of the first Test as well, to Kasun Rajitha. This time, it is his opposition skipper. Big blow to the Proteas. LUNCH ON DAY 1!

DRINKS! It has been a good hour for Sri Lanka as they have picked three wickets inside 13 overs. Two beautiful deliveries from Vishwa Fernando gave Sri Lanka the early breakthroughs which they were looking for. Another wicket came of a silly run out which the hosts paid the price for it. It was of Temba Bavuma. The onus will be on Faf du Plessis and Aiden Markram to steady the ship and take South Africa to safer shores.

Outside off, Markram leaves it alone.

FOUR! Probably the shot of the day so far! A very full ball on middle, driven with a straight bat all along the ground and beats mid on to his left. No stopping those!
Spraying this one down the leg side once more, this time Aiden connects his flick to deep fine leg for a run as he keeps the strike.

Short of a length outside off and going along with the angle, defended towards the off side.

Faf du Plessis comes in at number 5, way earlier than he would have expected.

OUT! Oh dear, oh dear... this is no miscommunication. No one called for a single, yet someone ran. Why? Everyone is asking. Length delivery on middle, Markram flicks it to mid-wicket. Temba Bavuma started to run but Markram does not respond. Actually, it was not even a run. It was a bit of a start. That is a problem with people like Bavuma. They look for singles everywhere and stop at nothing. So, after the start, seeing Markram's response, Temba stopped dead. Then, he casually turned back. As if to say, oh okay, no run there. But suddenly, he was caught on his heels as he saw Kasun Rajitha take aim at the bowler's end. Now, TB knows that he is in trouble. Starts to run but is too late. Rajitha's accurate throw hits the stumps. Almost the entire Lankan unit starts to celebrate, not even bothering appealing. But the umpire still refers it upstairs. Bavuma is not bothered either. He shakes his head and straightaway starts walking. He knows he is gone. And the replays confirm that Temba is really short. Well, about a yard from the crease. South Africa in shambles now. Poor cricket from Temba - too casual.
Good length delivery on off, Markram looks to push but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Full on off, Markram drives it to mid off where the fielder stops it brilliantly.
Left alone outside off by Temba. End of a sensational over from Fernando.

Close! But no hat-trick for Vishwa. A length ball just outside off and coming in slightly. Bavuma prods ahead to defend slightly. The ball goes off the inner half and bounces above the stumps as it rolls to the keeper. Almost! Fernando is on a roll here.
Temba Bavuma walks in next.

OUT! Gone first ball! What a ripper! Too good for even a batsman of Amla's caliber. A fuller length ball and coming in really late, Hashim barely has his eyes in and plays down the wrong line. The ball goes on to disturb the timber once more. Vishwa starts running and cannot be stopped by his teammates. Ends with a punch in the air! Two in two and Fernando is on a hat-trick now! For the first time ever Amla has got a golden duck in Test cricket.
Hashim Amla walks in at number 3.

OUT! Bowled 'em! This is brilliant from Fernando. He took the last ball away from the lefty on a length outside off but this time brings it in off a good length. Elgar was looking to drive that ball through mid off but the ball went in between bat and ball. It knocks down the off pole. The first strike for South Africa and Vishwa has shown good skill once more. Sri Lanka will be pumped up now!
Length ball outside off, kept out towards point watchfully.
FOUR! Along the ground and superbly controlled. A fuller length ball on the middle and leg stump line, flicked away by Elgar through mid-wicket for his first boundary.
On the pads and flicked away through square leg for a couple. It was slightly uppish but away from the fielder in the circle.

Peach! Should have had a wicket there! A length ball just outside off and shaping away very late, Markram looked to initially play that one but removed the bat out of the way at the last moment. That could have taken an edge!
Pushed towards mid-wicket from the crease by the right-hander.
A length ball on the middle stump, kept out well on the back foot.
Left alone outside off by Markram.
A length ball just outside off and jagging into the batsman. Aiden tries to keep the ball out off the back foot but is beaten and gets hit high on the thigh pad.

NOT OUT! That is a total waste of a review. Comfortably pitched outside leg. Fernando bowled a length delivery on leg, Markram looked to flick but got hit on the pads. Fernando appeals and is almost near the striker while completing the appeal. Really interesting to see the reaction from the Lankans though. Dickwella is the first to appeal but then bails out eventually. And Karunaratne - without even a look at Dikka, straightaway signals for the review! Well, at least he could have had a chat with his keeper. Too much of a hurry.

Review time... Sri Lanka have gone upstairs and Karunaratne has gone upstairs almost immediately, maybe making up for going really late in the last Test. The ball seemed to be pitching well outside leg though, could be an early waste of a review!

We are done with the national anthems and all set to begin. Dean Elgar and Aiden Markram walk out to the middle to open the innings for South Africa. Suranga Lakmal to start with the new ball for Sri Lanka.
Both the teams are out in the middle for their respective national anthems.
TEAM NEWS - The hosts have a solitary change, Vernon Philander who is injured walks out and Wiaan Mulder comes in. The visitors are unchanged after their victory in the first match.
TOSS - South Africa have won the toss and elect to bat first.

A warm welcome to the second and final Test between South Africa and Sri Lanka at Port Elizabeth. The hosts need to pull their socks up in this game to avoid a Test series defeat at home because of the loss that they suffered in the first game. But the Sri Lankans will know that it was all Kusal Perera's heroics which led them to victory. Now coming to this Test, the hosts need their batting to come good. Their bowling was decent in the last Test except for that last wicket stand which frustrated the South Africans. Overall, their bowling was very good. Vernon Philander has been ruled out of this Test as well. On the other hand, the visitors would be looking confident but would like to improve their batting as well. They know they just can't depend only on Kusal Perera and they will need other batsmen to step up as well. Their bowling has come good and they would look to continue that performance. The visitors will mostly not make any changes as they would like to go in again with their winning combination. Stay tuned for the toss...
